title: Streaming embeddings uploader with exactly-once delivery and async batch jobs
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Add a streaming and bulk upload path for the embeddings endpoint that supports large payloads, streaming line-by-line NDJSON, async job creation for heavy batches, idempotency keys for exactly-once semantics, and robust retry/backpressure behavior. This ticket covers API design, server-side queueing, storage of partial results, deduplication logic, client retry guidance, observability hooks, and migration/compatibility with existing synchronous endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/embeddings/stream accepts NDJSON stream and returns either streaming tokens or an async-job id for large uploads
Exactly-once: duplicate requests with same idempotency key do not produce duplicate vectors (dedupe within retention window)
Retries: clients can safely retry transient failures without double-processing; server provides deterministic status endpoints
Async job lifecycle: job states (queued, running, partial, failed, done) with progress percent and partial artifacts available
Backpressure: server signals ingestion throttling and exposes per-tenant queue depth and retry-after headers
Observability: metrics for ingest rate, dedupe counts, median latency for sync/stream vs async, and error breakdown
Integration: works with existing embedding storage and reranking pipelines; no regressions in embeddings generation quality
Rollout: feature gated and incrementally enabled per-tenant with telemetry for first 10 enterprise customers
infra_considerations: Requires adding a durable async job queue (Redis streams/Rabbit/Kinesis), short-lived blob storage for partial NDJSON uploads, and a dedupe index keyed by (tenant, idempotency_key) with TTL. Will validate memory pressure for KV cache and ensure worker autoscaling policies handle bursty bulk ingest.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only gate; run ingest against staging rerank cluster for 2 weeks
Beta: opt-in for 3 enterprise tenants with feature flag; monitor dedupe and latency metrics
Gradual: progressive traffic shift from sync endpoints to streaming for non-critical customers; 1% -> 10% -> 50% over 4 weeks
Full: enable for all tenants after 4 weeks and zero critical regressions
notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and SDK leads. Agreed to use Redis streams for job queueing; prefer short-lived S3 prefix for large NDJSON blobs.
2026-02-20: Decided dedupe window = 48 hours initially; store idempotency index with 72h TTL for safety. Trade-off: longer TTL increases index size but reduces risk of late duplicate acceptance.
2026-02-27: Prototype worker implemented to stream from Redis stream, validate lines, shard by tenant for concurrency. Early perf shows 15% CPU overhead on worker pods for 8k req/min workloads.
2026-03-03: Design review feedback from Security: must surface KMS ID of ephemeral upload artifacts and ensure ACLs for blob prefixes. Added security checklist.
2026-03-08: UX/SDK path: Node/Python SDKs will expose both streaming iterator and async-job helper that auto-retries with exponential backoff and attaches idempotency key by default.
2026-03-10: Canary started for internal alpha tenant; observed dedupe hits on test harness when replaying 500 duplicate receipts, behavior correct (no duplicates returned).
